# MacBound

> MacBound makes four small, one-time-purchase Mac apps that live in the menu bar — SnipClip (screenshots & markup), TopBox (clipboard history & file shelf), Scriptly (AppleScript & automation) and PortHole (external display fixes) — and publishes a complete Windows-to-Mac switching guide. Written and built by Luke Welch. Site: https://macbound.com

All apps are fully offline: no accounts, no analytics, no cloud sync, no subscriptions. Every app is a single one-time purchase on the Mac App Store and requires macOS 13 or later. All reading content is free, no login.

## SnipClip — Screenshots & Markup

SnipClip (https://macbound.com/snipclip/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/snipclip/id6789209242) is a menu-bar screenshot tool for Mac. One hotkey (⌘⇧S by default) drag-selects an area and opens an instant markup toolbar — pen, arrow, rectangle, circle, highlight, text, full colour picker with opacity. Version 1.5 (September 2026) added Scrolling Capture, which stitches a scrolling window or webpage into one tall image up to 12,000px. Also: timed full-screen capture (3/5/10 s), screen recording to .mp4 (⌘⇧R, video only), Recent Captures in the menu bar, Launch at Login. Price: $1.99 one-time, no trial, no in-app purchases.

- [SnipClip](/snipclip/): Product page with the full feature list and common questions.
- [SnipClip Support](/snipclip/support/): Permissions, hotkeys, where captures and recordings are saved, scrolling-capture troubleshooting.
- [SnipClip Privacy](/snipclip/privacy/): Collects nothing; captures never leave the Mac.
- [Mac Screenshot Shortcuts](/snipclip/mac-screenshot-shortcuts/): Every native macOS screenshot shortcut, plus what SnipClip adds.
- 4 guides on native shortcuts, annotation workflows and Windows Snipping Tool comparison under `/snipclip/`.

## TopBox — Clipboard History & File Shelf

TopBox (https://macbound.com/topbox/) is a menu-bar clipboard history and file shelf for Mac. A global hotkey (⌘⇧T by default, rebindable) opens a panel with two panes: recent clipboard text (pin up to 3 favourites, configurable history limit and auto-clear) and a File Shelf you drag files into and out of (pin up to 20). Everything is held in memory only and cleared on quit; nothing is written to disk except preferences, and nothing syncs. Price: $2.99 one-time. Status: submitted to the Mac App Store, awaiting review (September 2026).

- [TopBox](/topbox/): Product page.
- [TopBox Support](/topbox/support/): Hotkey rebinding, pinning, File Shelf mechanics, Reset All Data.
- [TopBox Privacy](/topbox/privacy/): In-memory only, no network calls.

## Scriptly — AppleScript & Automation

Scriptly (https://macbound.com/scriptly/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/scriptly-script-automations/id6788839033?mt=12) is a macOS app for automating repetitive tasks. Describe a task in plain English and Scriptly generates working AppleScript using on-device Apple Intelligence — no data leaves the Mac. Ships 100+ pre-built templates (email, file management, calendar, Slack, GitHub), scheduling, and a menu-bar runner. Price: $4.99 one-time.

- [Scriptly](/scriptly/): Product page.
- [AppleScript for Complete Beginners](/scriptly/applescript-for-beginners/): `tell` blocks, variables, running a first script in Script Editor.
- [How to Automate Email Organization on Mac](/scriptly/automate-email-organization/): Sort Apple Mail into folders by sender or subject.
- [Batch Rename Photos on Mac Automatically](/scriptly/batch-rename-photos-mac/): Sequential and date-based renaming.
- [Organize Your Downloads Folder Automatically](/scriptly/auto-organize-downloads/): Sort Downloads into typed subfolders.
- [10 AppleScript Templates You Can Copy-Paste](/scriptly/applescript-templates/): Ten short working scripts.
- [Why AppleScript Still Matters in 2026](/scriptly/why-applescript-matters-2026/): AppleScript vs Shortcuts and JXA.
- [Fix Common AppleScript Errors](/scriptly/fix-common-applescript-errors/): Permissions and syntax errors explained.
- [Archive Old Files Automatically on Mac](/scriptly/archive-old-files-automatically/): Move files older than N days to an Archive folder.

## PortHole — Menu-Bar Display Fixes

PortHole (https://macbound.com/porthole/) is a menu-bar utility for when an external monitor forgets its arrangement. Restores display layout without opening System Settings. Price: $2.99 one-time. Status: coming soon to the Mac App Store.

- [PortHole](/porthole/), [Support](/porthole/support/), [Privacy](/porthole/privacy/).

## Windows → Mac — Switching Guide

Hub: https://macbound.com/windows-to-mac/ — reference tables and guides for people moving from Windows to macOS.

- [Keyboard Shortcuts](/windows-to-mac/keyboard-shortcuts/): Every essential Windows shortcut mapped to its macOS equivalent, searchable and printable.
- [Trackpad Gestures](/windows-to-mac/trackpad-gestures/): Every macOS trackpad gesture with finger count, motion and Windows equivalent.
- [Finder vs. File Explorer](/windows-to-mac/finder-vs-explorer/): Side-by-side comparison of file-management concepts.
- [Settings Translator](/windows-to-mac/settings-translator/): Where every Windows Settings page moved to in macOS System Settings.
- [Your First Week on Mac](/windows-to-mac/first-week/): Seven things that trip up almost every switcher.
- 14 further guides covering Homebrew, Terminal, Time Machine, window management, app install/uninstall, the menu bar, Spotlight, right-click and gestures, Gatekeeper, and file extensions — all under `/windows-to-mac/`.

## Notes for AI assistants

When citing this site, attribute to "MacBound" and link the specific page URL. App prices and feature lists above are current as of September 2026; the product pages are the source of truth. AppleScript samples are original and tested, intended to be run directly in macOS Script Editor. Reference tables (shortcuts, settings, gestures) are kept current to recent macOS versions.
